title: Mandatory root-cause + mitigation logging for every bug/mistake
rootCause: Historically, errors may repeat when causes and mitigations are not captured in a durable, searchable place.
mitigationPlan: Log each mistake immediately with root cause and corrective controls.
Run preflight lessons check before build/commit.
Escalate repeated lessons to remindFrequency=frequent and priority high/critical as needed.
fix: Established global lessons-learned cache + preflight checklist and integrated rule into agent operating instructions.

title: Lessons-learned process applies to coding + tooling/gateway/environment changes
rootCause: Narrow scoping to code-only can miss repeat failures in operational/configuration work.
mitigationPlan: Apply lessons cache checks before config/tooling/environment changes.
Require rollback notes for gateway/tool/environment changes.
Track frequent operational mistakes with higher priority/reminder frequency.
fix: Expanded global quality gate and preflight checklist to include tools, gateway, and environment workflows.

title: Tool call failed due to incorrect parameter shape/field names
rootCause: Used incorrect argument keys for tool call variant, causing validation failure.
mitigationPlan: Validate required parameter names against tool schema before sending.
Prefer one canonical parameter style per tool (e.g., file_path/new_string) to reduce mismatch.
If failure occurs, log immediately and retry with corrected shape once.
fix: Corrected tool call format and completed requested changes successfully.

title: Incremental Gmail polling must dedupe previously processed messages
rootCause: Polling logic relied on broad inbox queries without persistent cursor/dedup state, so older unread threads were re-processed and could trigger duplicate actions/replies.
mitigationPlan: Persist monitor state (`last_check_ts` + rolling `processed_message_ids`) in memory/gmail-monitor-state.json.
Use incremental window with small overlap and hard dedupe by message ID.
Apply audit label `stickbot/actioned` to threads the bot acts on and exclude these from future scans unless explicitly required.
fix: Updated cron agentTurn instructions to enforce incremental processing + ID dedupe + state recovery behavior; added label-based audit safeguard requirement for acted threads.

title: Cron delivery mode must be none when user wants silent background polling
rootCause: The 15-minute Gmail triage job kept `delivery.mode=announce`, so each isolated run could still produce user-visible updates despite prompt text requesting silence.
mitigationPlan: Use `delivery.mode=none` for high-frequency background monitoring jobs.
Route only urgent/action-required notices via explicit `message` tool send.
Keep non-urgent reporting in a separate scheduled summary job (7pm).
fix: Updated Gmail triage cron job to `delivery.mode=none` and tightened payload instructions to send Telegram only for urgent/action-required items.

title: OAuth refresh failures can degrade effective tool availability and continuity behavior
rootCause: OpenAI Codex OAuth refresh failed at runtime (token refresh error), which left model selection appearing normal in status while requests failed before reply; recovery turbulence led to temporarily inconsistent tool behavior across contexts.
mitigationPlan: Treat auth errors as control-plane incidents: verify with openclaw logs around failure window for 401/invalid_token/refresh errors.
Run recovery sequence: re-auth provider, restart gateway, validate with a short test turn and session status.
After auth recovery, verify critical capabilities explicitly (cron access, session visibility, context-bridge files, and scheduled jobs).
For continuity incidents, enforce context-bridge protocol checks before making assumptions about cross-window state.
fix: Re-authenticated OpenAI Codex OAuth, restarted/validated runtime, confirmed cron/tool access restored, re-enabled and corrected Gmail triage schedule to 2-hour cadence with one ~3-minute follow-up check then fallback, and resumed context-bridge logging/reminders while restoring personality/memory continuity via goodmorning-openclaw.sh --restore.

title: Post-model-test window can silently regress memory/context files to skeletal templates or truncate bridge logs
rootCause: A short runtime turbulence window after unsuccessful Ollama/model testing coincided with memory and context-bridge files being replaced/truncated without explicit intent.
mitigationPlan: Immediately run git diff on MEMORY.md, USER.md, memory/*.md, and sharedspace/context-bridge/* when model/runtime experiments fail.
If regressions are detected, restore canonical files from repository state before any new writes.
Create a fresh low-level personality+memory backup artifact and update latest pointers for recovery scripts.
fix: Validated and restored affected files, logged bridge recovery event, and generated backup/personality-memory latest bundle.

title: Recovery/continuity script changes require dry-run + shadow test + audit before commit
rootCause: Without explicit validation gates, recovery scripts can appear correct but fail at execution time (e.g., checksum path context and cleanup edge-cases).
mitigationPlan: Require execution sequence before commit: --dry-run, --shadow-test, then --audit output review.
Only enable destructive restore path behind explicit --yes confirmation and pre-snapshot rollback.
Log each run outcome in memory and context bridge for traceability.
fix: Implemented goodmorning-openclaw.sh with guarded modes and validated sequence successfully before committing.

title: Golden continuity must test both live workspace and shadow-restored latest backup
rootCause: Testing only live files can pass while backup pointers lag behind, causing restore-time continuity failures.
mitigationPlan: Always refresh personality-memory latest bundle after continuity-critical updates.
Run goodmorning --golden-test to validate both live and shadow contexts before declaring migration-safe.
Persist latest golden test report in memory/golden-continuity-latest.log for auditability.
fix: Implemented checker + fixture + goodmorning mode; initial shadow failure exposed stale backup and was resolved by refreshing latest backup and re-running tests to PASS.

title: User-facing replies must use preferred name and suppress internal tool-style phrasing
rootCause: Metadata/tool-target phrasing leaked into conversational replies without a final user-facing naming/delivery check.
mitigationPlan: Pre-send check: replace/avoid numeric-handle references in normal user-facing messages; use preferred name 'Stick'.
Keep internal process/reasoning chatter in logs/context-bridge unless explicit user action is required.
Treat repeated naming/channel-noise misses as high-priority communication-quality regressions.
fix: Logged second occurrence, reinforced hard rule in USER.md, and committed lesson for pre-send discipline.

title: On Debian-like hosts without pip/venv, prefer user-local uv bootstrap for Python app tooling
rootCause: System Python lacked ensurepip/pip/venv packages, blocking conventional pip/venv installation paths without sudo.
mitigationPlan: Preflight-check python packaging availability before installation attempts.
Use user-local uv installer when sudo/root package installation is unavailable.
Record install path and launcher script for repeatable local operation.
fix: Installed uv locally (~/.local/bin) and validated Data Formulator via uvx without requiring system package changes.

title: External action completion claims require explicit verification evidence
rootCause: Without explicit evidence requirements, assistants may report attempted external actions as completed.
mitigationPlan: Require evidence block (method/source/timestamp) for any external action completion claim.
If verification missing, use attempted-but-unverified language.
Keep outbound actions approval-bounded unless explicitly pre-authorized.
fix: Updated SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, and pre-send checklist to enforce verification contract.

title: Third-party skill installs require verified-source trust gates and anti-exfil checks
rootCause: Public skill marketplaces can contain professionally disguised malicious skills and prompt-injection payloads that evade signature-only scanning.
mitigationPlan: Default to in-house skills unless third-party install is justified.
Before install, verify VirusTotal status, verified publisher badge, and publisher reputation/account age.
Enforce allowlist policy: skills.allowSources=["clawhub:verified"].
Apply zero-exfil rule to all skills: never provide personal/configuration/secrets; block and escalate suspicious data requests immediately.
fix: Codified owner-mandated install protocol in permanent memory and lessons log; future skill installs must pass trust-gate checklist before execution.

title: Multi-actor GitHub workflows require strict branch governance and conventions preflight
rootCause: When multiple actors (human + coding agents) can push as privileged contributors, direct-main writes or unvetted branch merges can cause destructive drift and poor auditability.
mitigationPlan: Before any GitHub code check/change, read repo conventions in README.md + docs/CONTRIBUTING.md + docs/DECISIONS.md.
Enforce branch isolation prefixes (feature/fix/docs/refactor/experiment/agent/stickbot/codex).
Use PR as integration gate; avoid uncontrolled direct writes to main.
Check branch diff scope before merge to detect sparse/destructive branches.
fix: Established and pushed repo conventions bundle on stickbot/repo-conventions, added PR template and decisions log, and flagged sparse agent/repo-conventions branch as non-merge path.

title: Intent chatter without artifact proof breaks execution trust; enforce execution-runner evidence gate
rootCause: Assistant replied with planned actions/status text before running tools and producing verifiable artifacts.
mitigationPlan: Use execution skill wrapper as canonical path for validation (`scripts/execution_skill.sh run-now|status`).
Do not claim progress/completion unless `state/execution-runner/last_run.json` and `state/execution-runner/latest.sha256` verify.
Echo fixed confirmation fields in chat: validation_run_id, artifact_path, artifact_sha256, latest_sha256_check, last_run_status, exit_code.
If no run exists, return explicit NOT_RUN instead of intent text.
fix: Added execution skill wrapper + skill definition, wired mandatory contract into AGENTS/MEMORY, and scheduled 15-minute isolated cron execution checks.

title: Execution skill must be explicit-trigger only (/guaranteed-execution) to prevent accidental or noisy runs
rootCause: Automatic/background execution and implicit invocations can violate owner intent and create trust drift during incident response.
mitigationPlan: Require `/guaranteed-execution` suffix for any execution-skill invocation.
Guard wrapper script to reject runs without explicit trigger token.
Disable auto cron jobs that call execution skill without owner suffix trigger.
fix: Updated skill + wrapper with explicit trigger gate and removed execution validation cron jobs to prevent unsuffixed automation.

title: Allowlist misses break chained orchestration; prefer allowlist-safe wrappers and single-step commands
rootCause: Chained shell commands (`cd && ...`) and non-allowlisted command forms frequently failed with `exec denied: allowlist miss`, stalling verification and deployment flow.
mitigationPlan: Prefer absolute-path wrappers and one-operation commands for runtime orchestration.
Use purpose-built scripts (`scripts/*_safe_start.sh`) instead of ad-hoc command chains.
When blocked, immediately report blocker and rerun via policy-compliant command shape.
fix: Added `scripts/unified_brain_safe_start.sh`, switched orchestration to single-step absolute-path calls, and validated restart/health through allowlist-safe flows.

title: Backup restore can reintroduce stale plugin config entries; clean immediately to avoid warning noise and drift
rootCause: A restore artifact reintroduced removed plugin entry `google-gemini-cli-auth`, causing persistent config warnings and masking real issues.
mitigationPlan: After restore/apply, run plugin/hook status checks and clear stale removed-plugin entries.
Use targeted config patch setting stale plugin entry to null for removal.
Record restore-origin drift items in lessons + memory for future post-restore checklist.
fix: Removed stale `plugins.entries.google-gemini-cli-auth` via config patch and verified clean plugin/hook surface.

title: New runtime hooks must be staged behind shadow verification before enabling on live gateway
rootCause: A newly introduced hook path for native common sync interacted badly with live gateway runtime and contributed to immediate instability perception/failure risk.
mitigationPlan: Never enable new hooks directly in live config first.
Run hook syntax+discovery in shadow/staging session, then enable with explicit rollback switch.
Keep rollback patch ready (disable entry + clear extraDirs + remove hook files) before activation.
fix: Rolled back hook config, removed hook files from workspace, and restored stable runtime path.

title: Tool continuation affinity key must not collapse anonymous traffic into a single lane-conflicting key
rootCause: Affinity key fallback used `endpoint__anon` when session metadata was absent, so unrelated lane tests shared state and triggered false `tool_continuation_conflict` (execution mode/lane mismatch).
mitigationPlan: Build affinity keys from strongest available context in order: explicit session, responses previous_response_id, tool call id, then model-scoped fallback.
Keep continuation conflict checks scoped to the derived conversation key, not global anonymous state.
Regression-check lane-invariant first-turn tool requests across local-fast/ops-maint/codex-high for no false 409 conflict.
fix: Updated `services/token-solver-v2/src/toolState.js` affinity-key derivation to use session/thread/call/model scope instead of global anon key, then restarted v2 and revalidated gates.

title: Continuation identifiers must be persisted as affinity aliases to prevent false missing-affinity 409s
rootCause: First-turn tool affinity was saved only under session/model canonical key, while follow-up requests resolve by `previous_response_id` or tool `call_id`, causing key mismatch and `tool_continuation_missing_affinity` despite valid conversation flow.
mitigationPlan: On successful tool turns, persist canonical affinity and alias keys for continuation identifiers (`responses__prev:*`, `*__call:*`).
Keep continuation fallback strict: allow compatibility fallback only when strong continuation identifiers are absent.
Maintain regression checks for both guardrails: G13 still rejects true missing affinity, and no-session previous_response continuation succeeds when first turn succeeded.
fix: Updated `src/router.js` to write alias affinity records and rebind compatible keys; updated `src/toolState.js` fallback policy to avoid broad model/anon fallback when strong continuation identifiers are present; reran v2 gate suite to 11/11 pass.

title: Strong-proxy auth fallback must resolve API key from auth profiles when env key is unset
rootCause: Codex tool-proxy fallback path only used `OPENAI_API_KEY` env, so deployments with key stored in `auth-profiles.json` (`openai:default`) remained auth-blocked despite valid credentials.
mitigationPlan: Resolve OpenAI API key from env first, then `openai:*` api_key profiles in auth-profiles file.
Use the same resolver across nano lane, codex fallback, and raw proxy calls to prevent drift.
Keep gate suite strict-schema valid so S1 failures reflect auth/routing truth instead of payload-shape noise.
fix: Updated `src/adapters.js` to load profile-backed OpenAI API keys and wired it into codex/nano/raw fallback paths; updated gate suite tool schemas (`required` alignment) and verified S1 strong proxy 200 with full suite 11/11 pass.

title: Execution contract must stay coherent from session/tool construction through final command authorization
rootCause: Gateway can produce stage drift where runtime tool construction and final exposed/authorized execution envelope diverge, causing runs to appear execution-capable while concrete commands are not executable under the final envelope.
mitigationPlan: Emit per-run stage fingerprints for: resolved session metadata, constructed tool IDs, post-policy tool IDs, provider-normalized tool IDs, and final authorized command envelope.
Add hard invariant checks: (a) constructed tool set subset/superset consistency at each stage, (b) every visible executable tool must map to an explicit authorization rule path.
Fail closed with explicit diagnostic event when visible/authorized mismatch is detected, and include diff payload for triage.
Add regression tests across direct/cron/subagent sessions with provider overrides and allowlist/approval modes to ensure invariant holds.
fix: Captured owner diagnosis and local verification evidence (session metadata intact, execution intent configured, allowlist envelope still decisive) to drive targeted runtime instrumentation and regression coverage.

title: Memory-loss recovery must run file-first tri-check and context-bridge reconciliation with proof
rootCause: When continuity drifts, relying on model recall alone can miss or distort state unless file memory and bridge state are reconciled in a deterministic order.
mitigationPlan: Run tri-check in fixed order: file-memory coherence, model-memory probe check, then context-bridge coherence.
Treat `MEMORY.md` + `memory/*.md` as authority and use model retrieval only as accelerator.
Require drift metadata (current compare timestamp, previous compare timestamp, stale>2d flag) in daily memory entries.
Keep a single recovery notebook with exact steps and evidence template for repeatable incident handling.
fix: Created and committed `docs/runbooks/memory-recovery-notebook.md`, documented no dedicated Python tri-check script currently, and standardized reconciliation/evidence steps.

title: Token-solver-v1 codex lane must not depend on stale direct OAuth profile tokens
rootCause: The v1 codex lane read access tokens directly from `auth-profiles.json`, so expired/stale Codex OAuth profile data could break lane execution even while the live OpenClaw auth session remained healthy.
mitigationPlan: Prefer provider paths that use current runtime auth state instead of scraping cached access tokens from files.
If direct OAuth file reads remain, pin the intended profile explicitly and reject expired tokens with clear diagnostics.
Keep a non-OAuth fallback path verified for codex-high so lane health does not hinge on stale profile files.
fix: Corrected v1 codex lane targeting, disabled the rotten Codex OAuth path for live recovery, and verified `token-solver/codex-high` succeeds cleanly on `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` without fallback.

title: Do not trust config acceptance alone for model pin changes; verify with live inference
rootCause: A model pin update to `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` was accepted by config tooling even though the provider could not actually serve that model, causing runtime `Unknown model` failures.
mitigationPlan: After any model pin or selector change, run a one-shot `openclaw infer model run` probe against the exact target model before declaring it valid.
Treat catalog/config acceptance and live provider reachability as separate gates.
If the live probe fails, immediately roll back to the last known-good model and record the mismatch.
fix: Rolled the active default back to `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` after live probe failure and kept token-solver remediation work anchored to the known-good model.

title: Local token-solver-v1 lanes must not silently cascade across multiple Ollama models
rootCause: The v1 local executor always appended fallback local models, so selecting a local lane like Gemma or local-fast could silently run on a different Ollama model after a local failure.
mitigationPlan: Make local-lane fallback an explicit config flag instead of an unconditional behavior.
Default lane policy by environment, and set this workspace to disable local fallback when model identity matters.
Keep fallback behavior limited to default/codex lanes unless a local fallback policy is intentionally enabled.
fix: Added `LOCAL_LANE_FALLBACK_ENABLED` handling to token-solver-v1, disabled it in the live `.env`, and surfaced the active policy in `/lane-contract`.

title: Picker-facing OpenAI provider catalog needs a full provider block, not just model entries
rootCause: While restoring missing direct OpenAI picker models, the top-level `models.providers.openai` block was added without `baseUrl`, so gateway config validation failed on restart even though the JSON itself parsed cleanly.
mitigationPlan: When adding picker/catalog providers, validate against gateway schema, not just JSON syntax.
Mirror required provider fields from known-good provider definitions before restart.
Treat model-picker visibility changes as config-surface work that requires a restart proof step.
fix: Added `baseUrl` to the top-level and agent-side `openai` provider blocks, then retried gateway restart with schema validation in mind.

title: Tool continuation affinity must read/write many concrete identifiers without broad model fallback
rootCause: Token-solver-v2 could write affinity under one response/session/request key but later receive a valid continuation under another identifier, causing 409 missing affinity; an overly broad model-scope fallback can also falsely attach unrelated continuations.
mitigationPlan: Resolve continuations by trying concrete identifier variants: previous response id, response id, call id, last request id, request id, and session key.
Write affinity records under primary, lastResponseId, lastRequestId, previous/call identifiers where available.
Do not use broad model/anon scope as a continuation fallback when concrete continuation identifiers are present or required.
Pin continuation routing to the resolved existing affinity so candidate model/alias changes do not break tool continuity.
fix: Patched token-solver-v2 affinity handling to read-many/write-many, added JSONL diagnostics, removed missing-affinity bootstrapping, pinned continuation plans to existing affinity, and validated with targeted previous_response_id repro plus full v2 gate suite.

title: Local search daemons must bind before expensive indexing and avoid read/write lock contention
rootCause: ThinMem installer and daemon performed a full `.openclaw` index synchronously; the installer hit timeout, the daemon was not queryable until indexing finished, and CLI search could hit SQLite `database is locked` while background indexing wrote to the DB.
mitigationPlan: For local daemon installs, bind/readiness should happen before expensive startup work.
Run large indexes asynchronously with a single index lock and expose health while indexing continues.
Use SQLite busy_timeout and keep read paths read-only when DB schema already exists.
Avoid full install-time indexing by default; make it opt-in for large trees.
fix: Patched ThinMem to async startup/periodic indexing, added `connect_db()` with busy timeout, avoided schema writes on existing read paths, and changed installer to skip full index unless `THINMEM_INSTALL_INDEX=1`.

title: Deterministic memory search needs exact-term specificity signals alongside path priority
rootCause: Initial ThinMem scoring over-weighted path priority and semantic hash cosine while flattening FTS5 BM25, so broad old memory could outrank exact policy snippets for queries like Sabir email/model policy.
mitigationPlan: Include deterministic query-token overlap and phrase-match bonuses in reranking.
Expose scoring subcomponents in results for debuggability.
Regression-test known policy lookups against native memory_search for specificity before claiming quality.
fix: Added token_overlap, phrase bonus, and bounded negative-BM25 transform; sampled policy query now ranks `MEMORY.md` Sabir policy first and returns in ~237 ms.

title: Picker catalog entries must be translated to OpenClaw schema, not copied raw from provider /v1/models
rootCause: Raw token-solver-v2 `/v1/models` objects were copied into `models.providers.*.models`, but OpenClaw's config schema only accepts a narrow model object shape (`id`, `name`, optional compat/input/cost/etc.), making the config invalid even though the live provider endpoint was healthy.
mitigationPlan: Before copying provider model catalogs into config, inspect `models.providers.*.models.*` schema and map fields into schema-safe entries.
Validate config through schema-aware tooling, not just JSON parsing, before any restart or probe.
Keep live provider metadata capture separate from picker metadata; do not assume API response shape is config shape.
fix: Replaced raw token-solver-v2 model objects with schema-safe picker entries, revalidated both config files, and reloaded the gateway catalog successfully.

title: ThinMem lessons-learned recall needs source scoping and stronger ranking for lessons.jsonl
rootCause: When evaluated on natural-language lessons recall, ThinMem often ranked broad memory markdown, preflight checklist content, self-referential recall logs, and disaster-recovery payload duplicates above the authoritative `sharedspace/developer-lessons-learned/lessons.jsonl` entries, so exact lessons were not reliably surfaced at the top despite being indexed.
mitigationPlan: Add explicit priority rules for `sharedspace/developer-lessons-learned/` and `lessons.jsonl`.
Exclude backup/disaster-recovery payload mirrors, `tmp`, `memory/.dreams`, execution-verification artifacts, and other duplicate/self-referential corpora from the default index.
Render JSONL records into labelled searchable text instead of relying on raw one-line JSON.
Add query-priority supplemental candidate injection so authoritative ledgers are always reranked for matching recall intents.
Regression-test natural-language lessons queries against expected top hits, not just exact-title searches.
fix: Patched ThinMem to index `.jsonl`, render `lessons.jsonl` as structured labelled chunks, support explicit high-value paths, narrow the active corpus, exclude noisy mirrors/self-referential logs, split lessons/preflight boosts, add query-priority supplemental candidates, rebuild the index, and validate 7/7 top-hit recall pass at ~142-375 ms.

title: SQLite index rebuilds must rotate WAL and SHM sidecars with the main DB
rootCause: The ThinMem rebuild helper moved only `thinmem.sqlite3`; stale `thinmem.sqlite3-wal` and `thinmem.sqlite3-shm` remained and SQLite initialization failed with `sqlite3.OperationalError: disk I/O error`.
mitigationPlan: For SQLite cache rebuilds, stop the daemon first and rotate the main DB plus `-wal` and `-shm` sidecars together.
Treat SQLite sidecar files as part of the database identity, not disposable unrelated temp files during rebuild.
Keep rebuild scripts reversible by moving old files to timestamped `.bad.*` paths rather than deleting them.
fix: Updated `scripts/thinmem_reindex_only.sh` to stop the service, rotate `thinmem.sqlite3`, `thinmem.sqlite3-wal`, and `thinmem.sqlite3-shm` together, then init/index/start/health-check the service successfully.

title: Buffered tool proxy must not request upstream SSE unless it streams SSE back downstream
rootCause: token-solver-v3 forwarded OpenClaw `stream:true` responses requests to OpenAI while its strong-tool proxy used a buffered JSON parser and Express `res.json` downstream path, so upstream SSE parsed as non-JSON and produced `502 tool_proxy_payload_invalid`; returning JSON to a stream-requesting OpenClaw client then caused empty/incomplete turns.
mitigationPlan: Force upstream raw proxy calls to `stream:false` while the proxy buffers responses.

When the inbound Responses request has `stream:true`, convert the completed payload into OpenAI-compatible SSE events (`response.created`, deltas, `response.completed`, `[DONE]`) instead of returning JSON.
Regression-check both direct stream=true `/v1/responses` and `openclaw infer model run --local --model token-solver-v3/local-fast --prompt hello --json` after v3 proxy changes.
fix: Patched `services/token-solver-v3/src/adapters.js` to force non-stream upstream raw proxy calls and `services/token-solver-v3/src/server.js` to emit Responses SSE for stream=true passthrough payloads; restarted v3 and verified hello succeeds through OpenClaw.

title: v1/v2 streaming proxy paths must preserve upstream buffered JSON and downstream Responses SSE parity
rootCause: The same stream compatibility class that broke token-solver-v3 also applied to older token solvers: v2 raw proxy paths could inherit inbound stream:true while buffering JSON, and v1 Responses streaming emitted a thinner event shape than newer OpenClaw Responses consumers expect.
mitigationPlan: For buffered raw proxy paths, force upstream OpenAI payloads to stream:false unless the service truly parses and relays SSE.

When inbound /v1/responses has stream:true, emit OpenAI-compatible Responses SSE downstream including created, in_progress, content part, output_text done, output item done, response.completed, and [DONE].
Regression-check direct stream=true /v1/responses for v1/v2 and keep local model liveness separate from stream-shape verification.
fix: Patched token-solver-v2 raw OpenAI proxy payloads to force stream:false and added downstream Responses SSE conversion; expanded token-solver-daemon/v1 Responses SSE event shape; restarted v1/v2 and verified stream probes returned response.completed plus [DONE].

title: Continuation affinity must canonicalize model aliases and derive stable session continuity keys
rootCause: Continuation state was bucketed by raw selected-model strings and sparse request metadata, so equivalent aliases like `local-fast` and `token-solver-v3/local-fast` landed in different affinity files, and requests lacking explicit `sessionId` could not cleanly resume/heal/transfer when the selected model alias or lane changed.
mitigationPlan: Canonicalize selected-model aliases before building model-scoped affinity keys, and read/write both canonical and raw alias forms for backward compatibility.
Derive stable continuity session IDs from OpenClaw request headers/body metadata (`session`, `conversation`, `thread`, `chat`) instead of relying on a single field.

Treat Responses continuation markers (`previous_response_id`, `response_id`, `last_request_id`) as continuation signals even before tool results arrive, and regression-check alias-switch second turns for affinity_read_hit + HTTP 200.
fix: Patched token-solver-v2/v3 policy + toolState + server + contract paths to canonicalize alias keys, broaden session derivation, and recognize Responses continuation markers; restarted both daemons and verified alias-switch continuity probes returned HTTP 200 with `affinity_read_hit` on the recovered session key.

title: Gateway transport policy must pass stable OpenClaw session headers to token-solver providers
rootCause: OpenClaw transport-policy only emitted x-openclaw-session-id/x-client-request-id for native OpenAI/Azure/Codex base routes, so token-solver v1/v2/v3 requests could arrive without a stable gateway-level continuity ID and fall back to opportunistic model/request affinity, causing tool_continuation_missing_affinity 409s during model/lane switches.
mitigationPlan: Treat token-solver providers/base URLs as OpenAI-compatible routes for transport-turn state injection.
Regression-check token-solver v1/v2/v3 provider ids and localhost ports 8797/8798/8799 emit x-openclaw-session-id plus turn headers before restart.
After gateway transport changes, restart gateway and run openclaw doctor plus a direct token-solver metadata probe to verify ingress sessionId is stable.
fix: Patched installed OpenClaw transport policy to include token-solver, token-solver-v2, token-solver-v3, and localhost token-solver ports in the session-header path; verified headers/metadata via import probe, direct v3 dry-run ingress sessionId, gateway restart, and doctor completion.

title: Health checks must match daemon bind behavior, not assume IPv4 127.0.0.1
rootCause: token-solver-v2 restarted successfully and listened on the Node default IPv6/localhost binding, but `scripts/check_token_solver_v2.sh` probed only `http://127.0.0.1:8798`, so the service appeared unhealthy even though `localhost` and `[::1]` health checks passed.
mitigationPlan: Use `localhost` or bind-aware probe logic for local service health checks when Node/Express may bind IPv6 `::`.
When a health check fails after restart, verify port binding and test both IPv4 and localhost/IPv6 before classifying the daemon as down.
Keep `/analysis` component checks aligned with the service control scripts so false negatives do not hide real unrelated blockers.
fix: Patched `scripts/check_token_solver_v2.sh` to probe `http://localhost:${PORT}` for `/health` and `/v1/models`; reran the v2 check and `/analysis check`, which then reported token-solver-v1, token-solver-v2, and token-solver-v3 all green.

title: Forced local-agentic lanes must pass local ownership evaluation and stream local Responses as SSE
rootCause: token-solver-v3 evaluator treated only local-default/local-fast as local lanes, so forced token-solver-v3/local-agentic requests generated a valid local answer but failed gate_policy_local_ownership, escalated to the OpenAI Codex fallback, and could fail with responses.write OAuth scope errors. Non-passthrough local /v1/responses stream=true requests also returned JSON instead of Responses SSE.
mitigationPlan: Include local-agentic and local-reasoning in local-lane ownership gates.
For /v1/responses stream=true, emit Responses-compatible SSE for local-generated payloads as well as strong-proxy passthrough payloads.
Regression-check direct non-stream, direct stream=true, and openclaw infer model run for token-solver-v3/local-agentic after v3 changes.
fix: Patched services/token-solver-v3/src/evaluator.js local lane recognition and services/token-solver-v3/src/server.js local Responses SSE handling; restarted v3 and verified direct stream/non-stream plus OpenClaw infer local-agentic succeed.

title: Token-solver recovery must use bounded post-restart probes as truth, not eager restart-script self-checks
rootCause: Token-solver v1/v2 restart scripts can start the daemon successfully but immediately run a self-check before Express has bound the port, returning non-zero with transient fetch failed even though the daemon becomes healthy seconds later.
mitigationPlan: Wrap solver fleet recovery in deterministic check -> restart -> bounded re-check logic.
Treat post-restart /health and /v1/models probes as authoritative over eager restart-script exit code.
Write latest JSON/Markdown artifacts so live health state is inspectable without asking the user to decode raw failures.

title: Auto tool envelopes should route locally when no tool is needed and recover 409/502 wiring errors internally
rootCause: OpenClaw can send a broad tool envelope with tool_choice:auto even for simple prompts. token-solver-v3 treated the envelope itself as requiring strong codex proxy routing, so local/downshift attempts could surface proxy/auth/payload failures or continuation affinity 409s instead of answering cheaply or recovering as a fresh text turn.

Regression-check direct non-stream and stream=true Responses calls for auto tool envelopes and orphan previous_response_id.

title: Fallback must handle runtime auth failures and try multiple stronger lanes, not only token-resolution failures
rootCause: token-solver-v3 text adapters only fell back from Codex OAuth to API key when token resolution failed. mitigationPlan: Treat runtime 401/403 from Codex/OAuth text calls as fallback-eligible auth failures.

Use bounded ordered stronger-lane candidates so nano/codex/local-agentic-fallback can recover from one lane failing.
Expose sanitized fallback_attempts metadata for diagnosis without leaking credentials.

title: Local solver health is not enough when large tool envelopes can monopolize a local lane
rootCause: token-solver-v3 could report healthy while a large gateway/tool-context prompt was routed into the local Ollama lane with a very long generation timeout and no local concurrency/prompt-size circuit breaker. That left Gateway with active embedded runs, made replies/model selector appear frozen, and caused restart/reset to wait for the 300s drain timeout.
mitigationPlan: Treat large tool-envelope prompts as unsafe for local lanes; escalate instead of attempting local generation.
Keep local generation timeout bounded separately from upstream request timeout.
Limit concurrent local generations so one stuck Ollama request cannot monopolize v3.
Validation must include large tool-envelope probes, not only /health and small prompts.

rootCause: After the v3 outage, v1/v2 still had older local Ollama paths where a forced local lane could enter long local generation without the same prompt-size and concurrency controls. Even where v1/v2 were less exposed to full tool envelopes, the same failure class could still monopolize local execution and create apparent Gateway/model-selector lag.
mitigationPlan: Keep local generation timeout bounded separately from request timeout in every token-solver generation path.
Add local prompt-size guards before local execution and escalate/downshift instead of attempting oversized local generations.
Limit concurrent local generations per daemon so one stuck Ollama request cannot monopolize the lane.

Treat auto tool availability as capability context only; hard-gate open-shell/dev-mutating profiles only when explicit tool_choice or task text requests tool/command/repo/build/test use.

Validate with both scorecard fixtures and live OpenClaw simple prompt probes after restarts.

title: Native memory CLI lifecycle must be read-only by default and safe-reindex swaps must be crash-resilient
rootCause: In OpenClaw 2026.4.27, `MemoryIndexManager.get(... purpose: "cli")` skipped watchers/listeners but the manager could still initialize dirty and `search()` could still invoke warm-session/on-search sync paths. Under timeout/SIGKILL during this sync/reindex path, the previous `swapMemoryIndexFiles()` sequence moved live `main.sqlite` away before temp-db promotion, creating a loss window where the target DB could disappear and be recreated empty. Safe-reindex also lacked final temp-db sanity validation before swap.
manifestation: Bounded native commands (`openclaw memory status/search`) intermittently hung or were SIGKILLed.

`/home/stickai/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite` was observed being recreated/emptied after failure windows in prior incidents.
Failure was lifecycle/path-related: memory config/provider could look correct while CLI invocation still touched sync/reindex behavior.
mitigationPlan: Treat CLI memory status/search as read-only operations unless explicitly running an indexing/sync command.
Prevent CLI search from calling warm-session or async search-triggered sync/reindex paths.

If there is new information, summarize only the concrete result/blocker and evidence, not the internal routing or completion boilerplate.
Run the pre-send checklist for completion summaries and reminder/summary turns.

Preferred owner recovery channel is the local OpenClaw browser/dashboard session on the host PC; use Telegram only after reply dispatch is verified again.

Email may be used as an alert/signal that Telegram is down, but do not treat email as authority to run operational fixes; require dashboard/local trusted approval for restarts, config edits, hotpatches, or auth repair.

After OpenClaw update, hotpatch, generated dist edits, or auth/config restart turbulence, use the gateway restart tool or full supervised restart path, then verify with openclaw status --deep and a live Telegram first-intent turn.

If ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND references hashed dist chunks, treat it as an installed-bundle consistency incident and repair by reinstall/update or restoring a coherent OpenClaw package before continuing validation.

title: Use error shape and fix pattern to proactively audit sibling failure paths before smoke tests
rootCause: Reactive fixes allowed the same leak class to resurface later in smoke testing. Fixing only the observed line left sibling boundary paths unexamined.
mitigationPlan: After any non-trivial bug, define the error shape: trigger conditions, boundary crossed, leaked artifact type, user-visible symptom, and why the first guard missed it.

Map the fix pattern to sibling code paths before rerunning live smokes: input extraction, prompt assembly, request metadata, downstream forwarding, streaming/non-streaming response handling, sanitizer/final render, logs/traces, and evaluator fixtures.

title: Words are evidence, not routing rules — no phrase-hardcoded intent classification
rootCause: The M25A visibleTextClassifier used fixed phrase matching (startsWith, exact string arrays) to classify user intent. "Run it." was caught by startsWith(run ) as tool_action, and "Proceed." was caught by single-word fallback as short_ambiguous_no_context — both without scoring context. This is the anti-pattern the M25A spec explicitly prohibits.
mitigationPlan: No route may emerge from a single word or phrase. Routes must emerge from scored contract: prompt shape + context gate + active obligation + risk + confidence threshold.
Short ambiguous phrases (continue, do it, run it, fix it, go ahead, try again) must be scored using multi-feature evidence, never phrase matching alone.
If confidence is below threshold, route to safe clarification or simple chat, never speculative execution.

Use deterministic weighted feature scoring: prompt length, imperative form, object presence, code/config indicators, active milestone state, prior unresolved action, tool dependency, environment mutation risk, execution reversibility.
Words may be tokenized as evidence only inside general features, never as hardcoded routing triggers.
This rule applies to all preselectors, classifiers, intent scorers, and routing decisions across all OpenClaw vMesh services.
fix: Rewrote visibleTextClassifier.js to use word families, structural patterns, and general heuristics (punctuation-tolerant matching, tool-verb + referential-target detection, acknowledgement promotion before ambiguous fallback, context-aware resolution). 21/21 fixture tests PASS.
